findings.title: Bind expiry-triggered refresh responses to the active session
findings.trigger: The refresh-expiry timer runs while access is still valid and calls getRefreshToken(). The user logs out or signs in again before that request returns.
findings.changed_cause: The candidate changes reconcileExpiry from opening the timeout path to starting an asynchronous refresh at refresh expiry.
findings.consequence: The response handler accepts Single-UI-Refresh without checking the initiating access token or session. A late session-A response can overwrite session-B refresh state. The next relogin sends the revoked session-A refresh token and clears the fresh session.
findings.next_action: Cancel the pending refresh during logout and reject a response unless its initiating access/session still matches the active store. Add before-login and after-login delayed-response assertions.
findings.validation: Run the fresh F03 before-login and after-login cases against the exact candidate, then run focused session lifecycle tests.
